claims.text: The material is an as-cast, solid-solution Co-free FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy.
Removing Co destabilizes dislocation cores in FeNiCrMn.
Removing Co enhances interactions between mobile dislocations and substitutional solute atoms.
Enhanced dislocation-solute interactions produce dynamic strain aging at intermediate temperatures.
Solute diffusivities are more active at approximately 400–500 K than outside this intermediate-temperature regime.
The proposed structural mediator includes dislocation pile-ups.
The proposed structural mediator includes localized solute atmospheres around dislocations.
Less-stable dislocation cores increase temporary pinning of moving dislocations by Fe, Ni, Cr, and Mn atoms.
Temporary solute pinning of dislocations induces dynamic strain aging.
Dynamic strain aging produces flow-stress peaks.
Dynamic strain aging produces serrated yielding.
The Co-free alloy will exhibit non-monotonic strain-rate sensitivity around 400–500 K.
The Co-free alloy will exhibit a flow-stress peak around 400–500 K relative to CoCrFeMnNi or to tests outside the proposed aging regime.
The Co-free alloy will exhibit serrated yielding around 400–500 K relative to CoCrFeMnNi or to tests outside the proposed aging regime.
TEM of the Co-free alloy deformed in the proposed aging regime will reveal dislocation pile-ups.
TEM of the Co-free alloy deformed in the proposed aging regime will reveal localized solute atmospheres around dislocations.
The proposed regime spans room temperature to approximately 700 K and strain rates from 10^-4 to 10^-1 s^-1.
A controlled comparison uses equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi tested under the same temperatures, strain rates, and loading modes as FeNiCrMn.
Deformation twinning may confound attribution of serrated flow solely to dynamic strain aging.

Absence of a statistically significant intermediate-temperature flow-stress peak and serrated yielding, or absence of pile-ups and localized solute atmospheres by TEM, is specified to falsify the hypothesis.
